newsitem.title: GERMANY: Solana says NATO will not offer Russia treaty.
newsitem.headline: Solana says NATO will not offer Russia treaty.

text.p: NATO will not offer Russia a formal treaty governing cooperation between the alliance and Moscow, NATO general secretary Javier Solana was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
In an interview with Germany's Die Zeit weekly newspaper, Solana said he was also opposed to Russia joining NATO.
"The NATO alliance does not believe a treaty would be the best way to solve the problems that have to be resolved," Solana said, according to an advance text of the interview released on Wednesday.
Asked about Russia joining NATO, Solana said: "It is not yet the right time for that. But NATO is an open organisation -- never say never."

Solana said he hoped that NATO could reach an agreement with Moscow on NATO's enlargement plans before its summit in July in Madrid. But he said the world would not come to an end if an agreement were not achieved.

"We would like to reach an agreement that would put relations between NATO and Russia on a lasting foundation," he said. "Russia should understand that we will do our best. But if an agreement can't be reached in time, we will postpone it and have to adapt to that."
